source.title: Beyond Importance: Interchange-Sobol Sensitivity Reveals Task-Specific Content Channels in Transformer Components
source.authors: Yi-Feng Guo; Jin-Hong Du; Xiang Chen

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and supplementary material are present
record.tranche_reason: Uses a different paired swap-versus-zero sensitivity method and reports IOI component outcomes bearing on evaluation sensitivity and a limited comparison with other attribution methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI layer-group sensitivity results and a prompt-level example, plus a statement that DLA and AtP* also rank AttnL9 near the top. It does not test the 26-head IOI circuit, its completeness or minimality, backup heads, or prompt-variant generalization. Figure 4 contains additional layer-profile values, but exact values are not stated in the text; they are not transcribed here. Factual-recall cross-task-donor results are not IOI behavior results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the IOI task from Wang et al. as one of three benchmarks for its own attribution method, IGSD. On IOI it reports only 24 layer-level swap-minus-zero contrasts, one illustrated prompt, and agreement with DLA/AtP*. It never maps results onto the 26-head circuit, its head classes, or backup heads. It also never evaluates the circuit's faithfulness, completeness or minimality. The IOI results are component-level sensitivity profiles for the authors' own method, a related but different construct. They go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, but IOI is secondary in the paper. The authors' main conclusion is that replacement and deletion are not interchangeable controls. Their headline evidence is from factual recall: an early MLPL0 relation-frame channel that standard scores under-rank, plus recovery of the AttnL9H8 head. IOI is used to show that the swap-zero profile is task-specific: roles flip, with late attention positive and MLPL0 negative. The authors make no claim about the IOI circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses matched-donor activation replacement paired with zero ablation and a Sobol-style variance contrast, rather than the original IOI circuit-discovery and patching procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: For IOI, the reported swap-minus-zero contrast varies by component; the paper also states that DLA and AtP* rank AttnL9 near the top. It does not systematically vary IOI prompt distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2 small IOI, IGSD finds the largest positive swap-minus-zero contrasts at late attention layers: AttnL9 +0.446 and AttnL10 +0.237. MLPL0 is negative (−0.122), and AttnL0 is flagged off-manifold (ST>1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At layer granularity, end-token IOI content sensitivity under matched-donor swap concentrates in layers 9–10 attention, where IOI name-mover heads sit. Replacement and deletion give different component profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: On one IOI prompt, swapping the AttnL9 output with a donor drops the correct name to rank #2. Swapping MLPL0 leaves it at rank #1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whole-layer late-attention swaps inject donor-name interference on IOI. This is a single-prompt illustration only.

record.problems: The reported IOI contrast values have no stated uncertainty here. The prompt-level illustration is a single example, and the study does not assess the full circuit's faithfulness, completeness, or minimality.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4's full IOI layer profile is not transcribed because exact values are not stated in the accompanying text. Appendix D.6 cross-task donor swaps use factual-recall recipients, so they are not IOI behavior results.

untested.parts: All: the 26 heads, 7 classes, faithfulness, completeness and minimality.
All: ablation of name movers and takeover by backup heads.
All. IOI is run only on GPT-2 small; the Qwen runs are factual recall only.
All: no circuit-discovery method is compared against the IOI circuit.
Circuit-level faithfulness and completeness under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions; the share of IOI behaviour the circuit explains.
All: no variation in name order, templates or number of names.

missing.what: A mean-ablation cross-check on IOI, stated to preserve the sign of the contrast at the focal groups. No numbers are given; tables are said to be in supplementary results.
The full IOI layer profile with CI shading and the off-manifold flag on AttnL0. This is figure-only.
An IOI donor used for factual recipients (cross-task swap). The recipients are factual prompts, not IOI behaviour.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V4 and V5 labels are rejected. The V5 label rests on layer-level sensitivities of the authors' own method, not on circuit faithfulness. The V4 label rests on a method-vs-baseline ranking comparison, not on circuit recovery. The AttnL9/L10 localization is loosely consistent with where IOI name-mover heads sit, but the paper makes no head-level IOI analysis or comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The 26 attention heads, seven classes, faithfulness, completeness, minimality, and stated patching roles of the IOI circuit.
Ablation of main name-mover heads and takeover by backup heads.
The same IOI circuit in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or other tasks.

Only a limited comparison of method rankings for the focal AttnL9 group is reported; whether other methods recover the full circuit, its classes, and roles, or whether ablation types and metrics recover essentially the same circuit, is not tested.

The study compares swap and zero sensitivity but does not measure circuit-level faithfulness or completeness, systematically vary IOI prompt distributions, or establish how much of overall IOI behavior the circuit explains.
IOI name orders, templates, prompts with more names, and whether those variants use the same components or heuristics.

conditions.value: "When Chris and Rachel went to the store, Rachel gave a drink to"

conditions.value: "When Chris and Rachel went to the store, Rachel gave a drink to"

rows.check: Single illustrative prompt, figure only. The rank drop from #1 to #2 after a whole-layer AttnL9 swap is not a measure of the IOI circuit or of name-mover roles.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small

rows.check: This compares the study's own method with baseline rankers (DLA, AtP*), which is method benchmarking and should not be a result row. No ranks are given. It is agreement among layer-level importance scores, not recovery of the IOI circuit, so it does not bear on V4.
